pattern: \bwhich buys most\b|\bthe two companies that buy (?:most )?conventional loans\b
struck: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the two companies that buy conventional loans, will not buy a loan in a non-warrantable building.
use: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the two companies Congress created to buy mortgages from lenders, will not buy a loan in a building that fails their project rules.

struck: A lender must re-check a Fannie-approved project's status at each loan.
use: A building's approval, or the lender's own certification of it, must be current on the day each loan closes.

struck: Hotel-type services, a resort name, resort marketing or a hotel rating also count.
use: Hotel-type services, resort marketing or a hotel rating also count, and so does a name with hotel, motel or resort in it, unless the word only refers to the building's past use.

struck: A purchase can be allowed when the owner holds 49 percent or less and is selling down.
use: Fannie Mae can waive the limit on a purchase that lowers that owner's share, if the owner holds 49 percent or less, is marketing units for sale, is current on dues, and the building has no special assessment.

struck: Minor suits are allowed: no money at stake, the insurer is defending, the HOA is a plaintiff over a minor matter, damage to one unit.
use: Some minor suits are allowed when the lender finds no effect on the building's safety, structure, use or livability: one over no money, one the insurer defends and insurance covers, or one over damage to a single unit.

struck: Critical repairs include unfunded repairs over $10,000 a unit due within 12 months.
use: Critical repairs include unfunded repairs over $10,000 a unit due within 12 months, not counting repairs an owner makes or repairs a special assessment pays for.

struck: For conventional loans with applications from January 4, 2027, the reserve line must be at least 15 percent of budgeted dues income.
use: Freddie Mac raises the test to 15 percent for applications from January 4, 2027; it says it made the change with its regulator and in alignment with Fannie Mae.

struck: Freddie Mac, and Fannie Mae in step with it, raise the reserve test to 15 percent.
use: Freddie Mac raises the test to 15 percent for applications from January 4, 2027; it says it made the change with its regulator and in alignment with Fannie Mae.

pattern: \bevery (?:attached )?condo loan\b|\ball condo loans\b[^.]{0,60}\bfull review\b|\bevery loan\b[^.]{0,60}\b(?:full review|reviewed)\b
struck: Every attached condo loan now gets the full review.
use: For most condo loans, the building's budget and reserves are now checked in a full review.

struck: Fannie Mae also checks the building's insurance itself.
use: The lender checks that the building's policy meets Fannie Mae's insurance rules; Fannie Mae does not review the policy itself.

struck: It reported 92 percent of the coastal market with private insurers and 38 percent of its own policies with a 5 or 10 percent deductible.
use: The state's wind pool insured about 8 in 100 homes in its coastal area in early 2025.

struck: Big percentage wind deductibles are common on this coast.
use: (cut it: the pool's deductible figure has no stated base and is not about master policies; give only Fannie Mae's 5 percent limit)

struck: One published program allows one owner up to 49 percent.
use: One published program lets one owner hold up to 49 percent, with conditions: units that come vacant must be listed for sale, not leased again.

struck: Of 11,822 condo units in the 45 oceanfront directory buildings the county records name, 545 units are taxed at the 4 percent owner-occupant rate. The middle building: 3.5 percent.
use: Of 11,471 condo units in the 43 directory buildings with a county count, 528 (4.6 percent) are taxed as the owner's home. In the middle building, 3.3 percent are.

struck: In 44 of 45 buildings, at least 75 percent of units are not taxed as the owner's home. At Maisons Sur-Mer, 72.5 percent are not.
use: By the county's tax records, at least three of four units in 42 of the 43 buildings are not the owner's home.

struck: 22 of the 47 directory buildings go by a name with Resort or a hotel brand.
use: 23 of the 47 directory buildings go by a name with Resort or a hotel brand.

struck: 8,375 of the 11,822 units (71 percent) have an owner mailing address outside South Carolina.
use: 8,092 of the 11,471 units, about 7 in 10, have an owner mailing address outside South Carolina, company owners included.

struck: Maisons Sur-Mer has the highest share taxed as the owner's home, 27.5 percent.
use: Maisons Sur-Mer has the highest share taxed as the owner's home, 27.8 percent.

struck: An FHA borrower signs that the home will not be rented for less than 30 days.
use: FHA will not insure a loan on a condotel, and it will not approve a condo building that is a condo hotel or has a required rental pool.
